resources.string: A mode is a group of overrides: the emoji row, the pinned tools and the symbol sets. A mode turns on automatically for the apps or the field types you select, for example password boxes and email boxes. You can also turn a mode on by hand from the Modes tool on the keyboard.
Let apps and field types switch the keyboard setup

Modes are off by default. When they are on, the keyboard changes its emoji row, its pinned tools and its symbol sets to match the app or the field you are typing in. Turn this off to use one setup everywhere. Your modes are kept, so turning it back on restores all of them.
Modes are off. The keyboard uses the same setup in every app. The modes below are kept and take effect again when you turn modes back on.
The keyboard saves a drag into the mode that is on

A mode that has its own pinned tools or toolbox order wins over the global lists while the mode is active. With this setting on, the keyboard writes the new tool order back into that mode. The change stays where you made it, and the apps on a different mode keep their own arrangement. With this setting off, a drag always changes the global order, and the list of the mode continues to override it.
The tool order can be different in each app. The mode that matches an app decides the order you see there.

When several modes match a field, the highest priority wins. Among equals, a mode with field hints beats one with field types, which beats one with only apps, and then the order in the list decides.

If you set apps, field types and hints together, all of them must match. For example, bind a mode to your chat apps and to the Text field type. The mode then stays off the search boxes of those apps. If you set only one condition, the mode matches on that one alone. If you set none, you can turn the mode on only by hand. When more than one mode matches, a mode that names hints wins over a mode that names field types, which wins over a mode that names only apps. A password box in a code editor still gets the password mode. A mode that you select by hand from the Modes tool wins until you change apps.
The mode goes back to the pinned tools, the toolbox order, the symbol row, the apps and the field types that it ships with. The app deletes your changes to the mode.
The mode and everything set up inside it goes, including its apps, its pinned tools and any overrides. This cannot be undone.

This is about picking a mode yourself from the Modes tool, not about a mode that switches on for an app on its own. Until you change app is the keyboard\'s old behaviour and suits a mode you reach for once. Until you change it suits a mode you meant to stay in, and it stays on until you pick another mode or turn it off.
Spaces the keyboard types for you while this mode is active

One switch over every space the keyboard puts in without a press: after punctuation, after a suggestion you pick from the strip, and after a word you glide. Off means every space in the field is one you typed, which is what you want when you are renaming a file extension, typing a command, or filling any field where a stray space is a mistake. On turns all three on, including the space after punctuation, which is off by default everywhere else.

Off makes every tap type exactly its key: a tap that drifts across the keys can no longer start a swipe. With autocorrect, suggestions and automatic spaces off too, this is a peck mode for codes, handles, slang and anything else the keyboard would try to fix.

On sends each key to the field the moment you press it, with no word held back. For terminals and code editors that show a word late. There is then no word for the strip to complete or autocorrect to fix.
On turns incognito on while this mode is active, with whatever you have set it to pause. It can\'t turn off incognito you switched on yourself.
Key-press sound while this mode is active, whatever the global switch says.
Key-press vibration while this mode is active, whatever the global switch says.
On makes Enter a line break in every field this mode covers, even where the app labels it Done or Send. Hold the key for the app\'s own action.
Off types each swipe as a word of its own, and a pause no longer ends a tapped word with a space you did not press. A word you are in the middle of is typed as it stands when the mode turns this off.
Which layout this mode types on

The mode wears this layout while it is on, whichever layout you were using before. Your own layout comes back when the mode ends, and the spacebar swipe order is not changed. Only layouts you have switched on are offered here; if you later switch one off, a mode that used it goes back to inheriting.
